limitations: A passed report proves inventory/result consistency and passing configured tests, not complete data quality.
Direct column coverage counts only column-level generic tests attached to that tested relation.
Relationships targets are distinguished from referenced parents; dependencies alone do not prove coverage.
Table-level and singular tests can cover more columns; their semantic coverage is not inferred from SQL.
No direct generic test can be intentional for nullable/descriptive fields or fields covered by GE/singular tests.
Declared source columns may be a subset of the physical source schema.
Baseline IDs detect additions/removals, not changes to existing SQL or generic test semantics.
GE expectations and source freshness are separate validations and are not counted as dbt test coverage.
